title: QA run · upgrade:ceremony (9/9) · 307ce4c4 · 2026-10-20 · 6 PASS / 3 PARTIAL / 0 FAIL / 0 BLOCKED / 0 NOT-RUN
body:
QA run record — 18.0 round-4 supplementary sweep, the #24681 targeted pass (18.x steps 5 and 6, the upgrade ceremony opened), record 2 of 3: the upgrade path, driven by hand, server side only. Framework `307ce4c4`. Maintainer-approved (dispatch session `session_01CfRDy7SuTfUqaTu2AEH2Hi`, 2026-10-20). Wave anchor: #24579. Previous round: round 3 at `580fd4ed` (records #24779 #24786 #24787 #24783). Sister records of this pass: `tier1:24681-touched` and `t2:24681-touched` (linked in the close-out comment).

## Environment fingerprint

- Framework: `307ce4c4b42503347d7f85825f572e4ca058b05f` (pinned, detached; no pull). No console build (`pnpm objectui:build` not run): every console leg is `not-run (console not built)`; `/_console/` answers 503 ConsoleNotBuilt.
- Container: cold tree. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (21 s), `pnpm build --concurrency=2` (76/76 tasks, 7m29s), `node scripts/check-dev-prereqs.mjs` green (70 artifacts).
- 18.0 code: two linked worktrees outside the main checkout, never a switch of the main checkout's sha:
  - `/home/user/os-next5` at `820fd5aef0` (the `@objectstack/cli@18.0.0-next.5` tag commit), `pnpm install` + `turbo run build --filter=@objectstack/dogfood --filter=@objectstack/cli --filter=@objectstack/example-showcase --concurrency=2`;
  - `/home/user/os-next3` at `2c9bf9430a` (`18.0.0-next.3`), same, plus `@objectstack/organizations`.
- Boots: `os serve` (production: `OS_DATABASE_URL`, own `OS_AUTH_SECRET`, 64-hex `OS_SECRET_KEY`), `os serve --dev`, `os dev`, `os start`, each started with `setsid` and stopped by the listener's process group; ports 41851–41858; never more than 2 servers alive. Every DB a file under `/tmp/qa4/` (SQLite), or a local PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster this run started (`qa4_n5`, `qa4_fresh`).
- Scratch apps: copies of `examples/app-showcase` (HEAD and next.5) for every leg that writes into the app directory; walled legs use scratch copies whose own `package.json` declares `@objectstack/organizations` and whose `node_modules` links it (RUNNER "A walled boot is a fixture of its own").
- Readers: row-level SQLite snapshots through `node:sqlite` (WAL included), diffed table by table over the columns the earlier snapshot held; `sha256sum` only after `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`.
- Runner: one parent session (this record). Independent verifier subagent for RULE 7 on the P0-adjacent finding (below).
- Timestamps (UTC, 2026-10-20): env prep 08:03–08:13; 18.0 worktrees 08:10–08:57 (in parallel); upgrade matrix 08:13–09:20; off-clause probes 08:49–09:15 (about 30 min of the run, below); core-item clauses 09:17–09:30.

## Scope

Selector `upgrade:ceremony` (a maintainer-named target, not a resolver selector). Judged: the 9 core items the dispatch names, each at its current revision (resolver: `node scripts/checklist-select.mjs ID --json` at `307ce4c4`):

|---|---|---|
| cli.organization-ownership-ceremony | 3 | P0 |
| platform-core.v18-boot-refusals | 5 | P0 |
| cli.dev-boot-contract | 5 | P0 |
| platform-core.boot-health | 7 | P0 |
| platform-core.seed-integrity | 3 | P0 |
| cli.migrate-plan-apply-json | 6 | P1 |

| identity-auth.self-service-password-reset | 3 | P1 |

Upgrade behaviour no clause names is in "Upgrade matrix" and "Off-clause probes". No item here is `planned`.

## Result

6 PASS / 3 PARTIAL / 0 FAIL / 0 BLOCKED / 0 NOT-RUN of 9. No clause failed. Three product defects were met beside the clauses and extracted (#24827, #24833, #24835); one open card still reproduces (#24638).

## Upgrade matrix

**a. Fresh install** (HEAD, empty SQLite file)
- `os serve` (production): "[organization-ownership] a datastore created from empty: birth marker written (shape generation 1, platform 18.0.0-next.5)"; ready; restart on the same DB ready. Marker: verified, `details.birth {shapeGeneration:1, platformVersion:"18.0.0-next.5", createdAt}`. A first boot that failed after the marker write (an invalid `OS_SECRET_KEY` of this run's own making) left the marker, and the next boot served.
- `os dev --seed-admin`: marker in the DB (the line is INFO; the warn-level dev log does not print it); restart ready.
- `os start -d … --home …`: birth line, ready; restart ready.
- First command `os migrate apply --yes`: exit 0, 71 tables created, `sys_migration` 0 rows; the first `os serve` is REFUSED, exit 1, "This database carries no organization-ownership marker: 17.x or an 18.0 pre-release (18.0.0-next.*) created it …". Reproduced twice. → #24827 (verified by an independent agent, RULE 7: CONFIRMED). `os dev` over such a DB is refused, then auto-runs the ceremony and serves, calling the DB "still in the v17 organization-ownership shape" (#24833).
- First command `os seed`: there is no such command (`os seed --help` → "Command seed not found."); `os migrate plan` first is harmless by code reading (it never flushes DDL), not booted.

**b. Real 18.0 databases**
- Generator: `node scripts/gen-upgrade-harness-fixture.mjs --ref …` does not run against either published pre-release (fixture gap below), so the 18.0 databases were made by the pre-releases themselves: each release's own `os dev --seed-admin` over a fresh file, then used through its HTTP doors (member invited and signed up, a second member by admin create-user, password reset, change-email, verification resend, two org invitations, global `mail` settings twice, tenant `branding`, the declared webhook activated, admin and member tasks, an admin sharing rule).
- next.5 (`820fd5aef0`), with planted rows the release cannot produce through `os serve` (a magic-link mail — 18.0 `os serve` hard-codes its auth plugins without `magicLink` — and five mail jobs): HEAD `os serve --dev` exit 1, absent-marker sentence naming `sys_flow_credential, sys_secret`; refused boot wrote 0 rows, no marker. Plan exit 0 (row diff 0). Apply exit 0, complete true, blocking 0; sibling-moves moved 11 (reset, two verification mails, the magic link; 7 global audit rows), jobsRewritten 3, activityRepointed 13; declared-webhooks mirrorsDeleted 1, activationRows 1; column-drops 2; not-null 62/63 (1 rotation shard unsupported). Data: moved rows byte-identical over the shared columns (mail 4/0 diffs, audit 7/0); both org invitations stay in `sys_email`; the pending `email.send.async` (reset, magic link) and running `email.attachment.reclaim` (verification) jobs carry `object sys_identity_email` in payload and metadata and the respelled idempotency key; the completed job and the org-invitation job untouched; no other row changed (NOT NULL lost none). HEAD boot: admin, member A (18.0 password), member B sign in 200, wrong password 401; A reads its own task; `sys_webhook` empty; one task PATCH → exactly one `sys_http_delivery` with `ref_id declared:showcase_task_changed`; the re-pointed send jobs completed without error.
- next.3 (`2c9bf9430a`), no plants: same shape; attribution 39 (next.3 wrote tenant setting-audit rows and an `admin_full_access` grant with NULL organization — single org, all to the one org), sibling-moves 10, mirror-deletion 2 (the two package sharing-rule mirrors; the admin rule `qa4_red_projects` kept), column-drops 2, not-null 62/63; HEAD boot and the same data checks pass.
- Declared-webhook deliveries: a real next.5 database holds none — on 18.0.0-next.5 the org-less declared webhook refuses to fan out an organization's event ("belongs to NO organization … refusing to fan out"). The delivery re-source was therefore measured on the committed harness fixture (main `5b14b7f3` data), production composition: deliveriesResourced 2 (`ref_id whk_… → declared:showcase_task_changed`), and HEAD's outbox picked both up under the declaration (attempts 3; `hooks.example` is unreachable here).

**c. v17 shape** (R3: `sys_metadata.organization_id` added to the next.5 database) — refused (names `sys_metadata` among the three tables), drop gate holds, plan changes nothing, apply complete, `sys_metadata.organization_id` dropped, boot 200 (clause evidence above).

**d. Developer's local database** (scratch app directory; next.5 `os dev` with nothing chosen created `.objectstack/data/objectstack.db`; then the app's code swapped to HEAD, `.objectstack/` kept)
- HEAD `os dev` (nothing chosen) upgraded it in place and served (health 200 after 27 s): backup at `.objectstack/data/backups/organization-ownership-TIMESTAMP/` holding both databases, plan, report and ceremony log; admin, members (18.0 passwords), own data, mail moves and the webhook all check out.
- What the developer reads, in order: two `[schema-drift] sys_secret.organization_id / sys_flow_credential.organization_id … "os migrate apply --allow-destructive" to drop it` lines (#24638, still reproduces); an ERROR line with the refusal's stack; "⟳ This development database is still in the v17 organization-ownership shape — upgrading it in place (a copy is kept first)…" (#24833); "✓ Upgraded … copied to …"; "✓ server started on the upgraded database". The outcome is right; the account of it is wrong in two places.

**e. Walled** (`isolated` and `group`)
- HEAD fresh walled boot (scratch app declaring the runtime): Tenancy isolated, Organizations mounted, birth marker written.
- 18.0 walled database: 18.0.0-next.3 (it predates next.5's walled-boot refusal) under `OS_TENANCY_POSTURE=isolated` with `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL` and `OS_AUTH_MEMBERSHIP_POLICY=invite-only`; two organizations (`/auth/organization/create`), one member each (admin create-user → change-password → invite → accept), per org an admin task, a member task, an unaccepted invitation, a branding setting, a password reset and an admin sharing rule. next.3 wrote every tenant setting-audit row with organization_id NULL.
- isolated: refused; plan posture isolated, 3 organizations, unattributable `sys_setting_audit` 3 ("no anchor names the owner"); apply exit 1, complete true, blocking 3, held with the remedy "assign each row its organization … or delete it by hand, then re-run --apply; the ceremony never guesses an owner and never deletes such a row". After the operator's assignment (this run matched each row's `new_hash` to its organization's current setting value) the re-apply certified (blocking 0). HEAD boot: Alice (org A) and Bob (org B) sign in with their 18.0 passwords; each sees exactly its own organization's two QA4 tasks (foreign rows 0); the other organization's task → 404; own task 200; members → 403 on `sys_identity_email` and `sys_email`. Whole-DB row diff: organization_id null→value 3 (exactly the operator's), value→another organization 0.
- group: identical outcome (3 held, assigned, certified, same isolation results, 0 rows moved across organizations).
- `os dev` over the unassigned walled DB: prints the held table and "✗ Every step finished, and the post-check found 3 row(s) left … not certified … Resolve them, then run `os migrate organization-ownership --dev --apply --plan-file … --backup-taken` — or restore the copy", exit 1, nothing listening.
- No cross-organization mismatch was found.

## Off-clause probes

About 30 minutes of the run (08:49–09:15 plus the PostgreSQL leg).

- **Kill mid-apply, then re-run.** SIGKILL at 3.5 / 4.3 / 4.8 / 5.0 / 5.1 / 5.3 s into `--apply` on the planted next.5 database. Up to 4.8 s no checkpoint existed and the boot refused with the absent-marker sentence; from 5.0 s an unverified checkpoint existed and the boot refused with "The organization-ownership ceremony has not finished on this database … not verified". In every case re-running `--apply` with the same plan completed (blocking 0), with 0 mail ids lost, 0 duplicated, jobs re-pointed once, and the next boot served. No kill landed inside sibling-moves (under 0.2 s on this DB); simulated instead — a reset row copied into `sys_identity_email` and not deleted — the re-run reported moved 10, alreadyMoved 1, one copy, nothing left behind. Neither a half-upgraded servable database nor data loss was found.
- **Re-run on a certified database.** Plan and apply exit 0, every step `checkpointed`, row diff 0 apart from the marker's timestamps — a no-op. On a birth-marker database every step runs `done` with row diff 0, and the marker's `details.birth` is replaced by a checkpoint (observation below).
- **Lower shape generation (F5).** Simulated (generation removed / set to 0 on a certified marker) and real: 18.0.0-next.3 ships an open generation-0 ceremony; its own plan/apply certified the next.3 database without `shapeGeneration`; HEAD then refused it, exit 1: "This database was certified by an organization-ownership ceremony of shape generation 0, and this release requires generation 1: the ceremony steps added since have not run on it. sys_flow_credential, sys_secret still carry …". HEAD's ceremony then re-ran every step (sibling-moves 10, mirror-deletion 2, column-drops 2, not-null 62/63), certified, and the data checks pass.
- **Telemetry sibling.** A fresh primary next to a leftover 18.0 telemetry sibling (113 audit rows) was born and served; an old primary with no sibling was still refused and got no marker. Holds both ways.
- **driver-sql vs driver-turso.** PostgreSQL 16.15 (SqlDriver(pg), local): next.5 database on PG → refused → ceremony complete (not-null 63/63, 0 unsupported — SQLite reports 1 unsupported rotation shard) → boot and data checks pass; but the declared webhook never enqueues on PostgreSQL, fresh install included → #24835. driver-turso (TursoDriver(libsql), local file): fresh boot born and restarted; the next.5 file under the turso driver refused → ceremony complete (not-null 62/63) → boot and data checks pass; activityRepointed 0 there because the turso composition mounts no telemetry sibling while this file's activity rows live in the SQLite composition's sibling (mixed fixture). Turso remote face, MySQL, MongoDB: blocked(fixture) — none provisioned.
- **Exit codes and `--json`.** `os serve` refusal exit 1 (no `--json` on serve). Ceremony `--json`: plan exit 0, stdout one JSON value `{file, plan}`; every refusal exit 1 with stdout one JSON value `{error:"apply_refused", reason, detail[, file, reviewed, current]}` — no plan file, missing plan file, no `--backup-taken`, a plan computed for another database ("…was computed for the database …/n3.db, and this run opened …/n5.db. Nothing was written."); held rows exit 1 with the report. Drop gate `--json` exit 1 `{message:"refused_organization_ownership_unmigrated", tables, detail, marker}`. `os dev` with held rows exit 1, nothing listening. These match PR #24681's stated shapes.

## Defects extracted (reproduction rules in each card)

- #24827 — `os migrate apply --yes` on an empty database writes no birth marker; the first `os serve` refuses the fresh install as a 17.x / 18.0 pre-release database. Repro: `os migrate apply --yes --database-url file:NEW.db` (exit 0, 71 tables, `sys_migration` 0 rows) → `OS_DATABASE_URL=file:NEW.db os serve` → exit 1, absent-marker sentence; expected: served. Reproduced twice; RULE 7 verifier CONFIRMED from the evidence and the code (deferred-DDL boot reports 0 tables created; nothing records the birth after `flushSchemaDdl()`).
